newsitem.title: USA: UAW 1996 receipts drop 42 percent since 1978.
newsitem.headline: UAW 1996 receipts drop 42 percent since 1978.

text.p: The amount of money taken in by the United Auto Workers union last year was nearly 42 percent less on an inflation-adjusted basis than what it received in 1978, according to an analysis published Sunday by The Detroit News.

The UAW took in total receipts -- including dues, fees, interest, dividends and proceeds from asset sales -- of $303.5 million in 1996. That is down 41.8 percent after inflation from 1978, according to calculations done by Comerica Bank for the newspaper.

During the same period, dues fell 50 percent adjusted for inflation, as the union's membership has fallen to 742,454 in 1996 from 1.5 million in 1979. The newspaper did not provide dollar figures for 1978 total receipts or for dues in the two periods.

The paper, citing UAW filings with the U.S. Labor Department, also said the union's strike fund totaled $859.6 million in 1996, a 13 percent drop from 1992. One reason for the decline was $365.9 million paid to striking workers over the last five years, including $184.3 million paid during 1995 during a Caterpillar Inc. strike.

The newspaper reported the UAW has lost 204,992 potential new members because of failed organizing efforts over the last 17 years. But the union has gained 109,576 new members through elections in areas such as South Carolina, Indiana and Tennessee.

The story detailed challenges facing the union as it battles to organize new workers and combat continuing efforts by the Big Three U.S. automakers -- General Motors Corp., Ford Motor Co.. and Chrysler Corp. -- to cut their work forces to gain efficiencies. UAW offices were
closed for the weekend, and officials could not be reached for comment.
